module.purpose: Provides Turbopack-specific React Flight client configuration: resolving client/server references, preparing destinations, preloading and requiring modules via Turbopack chunk loading, and gathering debug info.
module.summary: This module bridges React Flight client-side reference metadata with Turbopack's module system. It exports functions to resolve client and server references into internal tuples, preload module chunks asynchronously, require modules (suspending if needed), and collect dev debug info. It uses WeakSets to track instrumented and loaded chunk promises, avoiding duplicate instrumentation. Opaque types hide metadata shape from consumers. It depends on external helpers from react-client and shared import metadata.
module.businessContext: Part of React Server Components bundler integration for Turbopack. Enables client to load server/client references. Failure breaks module loading in RSC.

const instrumentedChunks: WeakSet<Thenable<any>> = new WeakSet();

detail.name: ignoreReject
preconditions: The `promise` parameter must be a valid Promise instance or thenable object.
postconditions: Returns a promise that resolves once the input promise settles, regardless of whether it fulfilled or rejected.
invariants: The returned promise will never reject under normal operation.
edgeCases: If the input promise resolves, the returned promise resolves immediately.
If the input promise rejects, the rejection is absorbed and no error propagates to the caller.
If a non-promise thenable is passed, it is treated equivalently to a native Promise.
detail.summary: Accepts a promise and handles its rejection silently, preventing unhandled rejection warnings without blocking execution.

detail.signature: export function preloadModule<T>(metadata: ClientReference<T>): null | Thenable<any>
preconditions: metadata must contain a valid CHUNKS array of chunk filenames
metadata may optionally be an async import
postconditions: all chunk files are loaded via loadChunk
instrumentedChunks tracking is updated for each loaded chunk
loadedChunks registry is populated
returns null if no chunks and not async import
returns a thenable if chunks or async imports remain pending
invariants: loadedChunks and instrumentedChunks Sets remain consistent across calls

units.name: requireModule

detail.name: requireModule
preconditions: metadata argument must be a valid ClientReference<T> object containing at least the ID key used to resolve the module via __turbopack_require__.
postconditions: Returns the resolved module export or sub-property identified by metadata[NAME].
For async imports, returns the fulfilled value once the promise is resolved.
For metadata[NAME] === '*', returns the full module exports object unchanged.
For metadata[NAME] === '', returns the default export if __esModule is truthy, otherwise the full module exports.
edgeCases: metadata[NAME] === '*': treats the module as a CommonJS import and returns the entire moduleExports object.
metadata[NAME] === '': assumes ESM interop and returns moduleExports.__esModule ? moduleExports.default : moduleExports.
hasOwnProperty.call(moduleExports, metadata[NAME]) is true after name checks
Async import where moduleExports.then is not a function indicates the module was not actually a promise (placeholder path).
Async import with status === 'fulfilled' yields moduleExports.value as the resolved value.
Async import in rejected state rethrows moduleExports.reason.

raises: Re-throws moduleExports.reason if the async promise is in a rejected state.

detail.name: getModuleDebugInfo
detail.signature: export function getModuleDebugInfo<T>(metadata: ClientReference<T>): null | ReactDebugInfo
preconditions: metadata must conform to ClientReference<T> structure
metadata[CHUNKS] must exist when __DEV__ is true
Each chunk must either be a plain tuple or a merged chunk [mergedChunkFilename, ...]
postconditions: Returns null when __DEV__ is false
Returns array of ReactDebugInfo entries when __DEV__ is true
Each debug info entry contains filename and id derived from chunk data
Merged chunks use their own filename instead of the client reference filename
invariants: Return type is strictly null | ReactDebugInfo
Only executes chunk processing logic when __DEV__ is true
All chunk entries are processed exactly once in order
edgeCases: When __DEV__ is false, immediately returns null bypassing all chunk logic
Merged chunks (arrays starting with [mergedChunkFilename, ...]) are identified and their filename is used
Chunks without explicit filename fall back to ClientReference filename
detail.summary: Extracts React debug information from a client module reference's chunks in development mode, returning null in production builds.
